title: Melchizedek's Canaanite territory and the Melchizedekian heresy
english: That Melchizedek is shown to be Canaanite by descent can be inferred from the very regions he ruled and reigned over, and from the places he lived near. He was a neighbor of Sodom, and he was closer still to Abraham, who was living by the oak of Mamre (Genesis 18:1). And I think he was also king of Salem—that is, of this much-talked-of Jerusalem.

So if Melchizedek clearly resembles the Son of God, he will not be without father or without mother or without genealogy. Instead, the things of the flesh will be traced in a genealogy according to the nature of the flesh, and the other part will be seen as without genealogy, just as is certainly the case also with Christ. For Christ is traced in a genealogy according to the body, but according to the highest order he has his descent indescribable, as we have previously explained.

From Chrysostom on this same passage: Many who did not understand what was said about Melchizedek have said that he was greater than Christ, and they established for themselves a heresy; they are also called Melchizedekians. So, contending and wanting to show that Melchizedek is greater than Christ, they bring forward to us as witness the Scripture that says, “You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek” (Psalm 109:4 (Psalm 110:4 in Hebrew numbering)). For how, they say, would he not be greater, the one according to whose image and order Christ serves as priest? But others, having gone astray, say that he is the Holy Spirit.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Eustathius has just argued that Scripture calls Melchizedek without father and without mother because his Canaanite ancestors were unworthy; he now gives territorial evidence for Melchizedek's Canaanite origin, then quotes Chrysostom reporting the Melchizedekian heresy.

title: Melchizedek is human, not greater than Christ, and his missing genealogy is a type
english: But we say that he was a human being with feelings like ours, not greater than Christ—nor even greater than John the Baptist—and certainly not the Holy Spirit. As for the claim that he is greater than Christ, let those who say this tell us: what region do they say he belongs to? Is it heavenly? Is it earthly or under the earth? If it is heavenly or some other region, let them hear that to him every knee will bend, and so on (Philippians 2:10). If every knee bends, then the one who worships would be less than the Christ who is worshipped. But the wretched people do not even know the next line: “being made like the Son of God”—just as we also came into being according to the image and likeness of God (Genesis 1:26).

But perhaps one of the hearers asks and says: What then does it mean that he is called without father, without mother, and without genealogy? To him we will answer that the Jews have said he was born of a prostitute, and for that reason Scripture did not trace his genealogy. To them we will answer: You have spoken wrongly. For we find others who were born of a prostitute and yet had their genealogy traced—immediately Solomon, born of Uriah’s wife, and then Abimelech, the son of Gideon. Why then is his genealogy not traced? Because he was a type of Christ and bore his image. For this reason Scripture omitted his father and mother, so that in him, as in an image, we might behold as in a mirror the Christ who is truly without father, without mother, and without genealogy.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Chrysostom is reporting the orthodox reply to those who said Melchizedek was greater than Christ or was the Holy Spirit, and to Jews who said he was born of a prostitute.

title: Christ the true Melchizedek: without father on earth, without mother in heaven
english: For Christ is without father on earth according to the flesh, and without mother in the heavens according to the spirit, according to the divinity. Such also is the one who has neither beginning of days nor end of life. Scripture did not trace a genealogy for Melchizedek, but omitted his birth and his death, so that, as we said before, we might behold this one in him. For Melchizedek is interpreted as king of righteousness, who is Christ, having neither beginning of days nor end of life. The Word of God was neither begotten at a beginning of days, nor did he ever cease or come to an end, for Christ remains forever.

So Melchizedek was a righteous man and truly bore the image of God in himself. Moved therefore by prophetic spirit, he understood the offering that was to be brought to God by Christ, and he honored God with bread and wine, imitating the Christ who was to come. Since in the synagogue of the Jews the order of Aaron offered sacrifice to God—not bread and wine, but calves and lambs, glorifying God with bloody sacrifices—God cried out to Jesus, who was to be born from the virgin Mary, saying: You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek (Psalm 109:4), not according to Aaron, who served with bloody sacrifices, but according to the order of Melchizedek, bringing the offering of the nations in bread and wine perpetually.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Eustathius is closing his treatise by explaining how Melchizedek's unrecorded genealogy points to Christ, who alone is truly without father on earth and without mother in heaven.
